compiled:
📰 General

Trump Announces Renaming of Kennedy Center to "Trump-Kennedy Center" •

The White House confirmed Thursday that former President Donald Trump has requested and secured approval to rename the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts as the “Trump-Kennedy Center.” This decision follows a recent request from Trump to commemorate his time in office. The renaming will be officially implemented, marking a significant shift in the center’s identity. The move has drawn criticism from some quarters, while supporters celebrated the recognition.

🌍 World

Guggenheim Museum Abandons Basque Country Expansion Following Local Opposition •

The Guggenheim Museum has withdrawn its plans to construct a satellite location in the Basque Country. This decision follows sustained protests from environmental groups and local campaigners concerned about the project’s impact on a UNESCO biosphere reserve. The area is a crucial habitat for wildlife and migratory birds, prompting significant opposition to the museum’s expansion. Authorities cited the strong local resistance as the primary reason for abandoning the ambitious project.

🦅 US

EU Announces Significant Asylum Restrictions Targeting Seven Countries •

The European Union announced a plan to significantly limit asylum claims originating from Colombia, India, Egypt, Albania, Sudan, Lebanon, and Bangladesh. The decision, effective immediately, classifies these nations as “safe countries of origin,” triggering immediate scrutiny and condemnation from numerous human rights organizations. The EU’s rationale centers on a new assessment of risks associated with asylum applications from these countries. This move represents a substantial shift in the EU’s approach to asylum processing and raises concerns about potential human rights implications.

💰 Business

Trump Media and Google-Backed Fusion Firm Announce $6 Billion Merger •

Trump Media & Technology Group is merging with TAE Technologies, a fusion energy company backed by Google’s parent company, Alphabet. The proposed deal values Trump Media at $6 billion, primarily driven by the company’s ownership of Truth Social. The merger aims to leverage TAE Technologies’ expertise in fusion energy with Trump Media’s digital platform. Financial details and the specific integration strategy are currently under discussion as the deal progresses through regulatory approvals.

💻 Technology

Riot Games Discovers Motherboard Flaw, Leading to BIOS Updates for Cheater Prevention •

Riot Games identified a security vulnerability in several recent motherboard designs that could allow PC cheaters to operate undetected. The flaw relates to how the motherboard handles system interrupts, providing a method for bypassing anti-cheat software. Asrock, Asus, Gigabyte, and MSI have released BIOS updates to patch the vulnerability, addressing the potential for exploitation. These updates mitigate the risk of cheaters gaining an unfair advantage within Riot’s games.

🎭 Entertainment

Tom Cruise and Alejandro G. Iñárritu Unveil Title of New Film: “Digger” •

Warner Bros. and Tom Cruise have announced the title of the upcoming film directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu as “Digger.” The film is slated for release on October 2, 2026. A Saul Bass-inspired promotional poster was shared to announce the title. Details regarding the film’s plot and cast remain undisclosed at this time.

🏅 Sports

Dolphins Exploring Tua Tagovailoa Trade Options Ahead of 2026 Season •

The Miami Dolphins are reportedly considering options for quarterback Tua Tagovailoa’s future, with a potential trade becoming increasingly likely. The team is exploring a post-June 1 designation, which would allow them to release Tagovailoa without incurring a significant penalty. This move would activate a compensation package of $99.2 million. The Dolphins’ plan involves initiating this process following the conclusion of the 2025 season. The team is currently evaluating the potential return they could receive for the veteran quarterback.

🔬 Science

Perseverance Rover’s Longevity on Mars to Be Tested in Upcoming Mission •

NASA is anticipating crucial data regarding the Perseverance rover’s operational capabilities on Mars within the next few years. The agency’s projections for the next American lander’s arrival have been significantly delayed, creating a window for Perseverance to demonstrate its continued functionality. Scientists will be closely monitoring the rover’s performance, particularly its ability to maintain power and navigate challenging terrain. This extended mission aims to assess the long-term viability of robotic exploration on the planet.

🩺 Health

Michigan Drops Kennedy-Appointed Vaccine Council, Returning to Standard Guidelines •

Michigan’s Department of Health and Human Services has announced a change in its approach to vaccine recommendations for children. The department is now advising healthcare providers to adhere to vaccine schedules established by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) or the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP). This decision reverses a previous arrangement where a council appointed by former Governor Gretchen Whitmer provided specific vaccine guidance. The shift reflects a move towards established medical organizations’ recommendations and reduces the influence of the previously formed advisory group. The change was effective immediately following the department’s announcement.
